strategies.name: Test trunc with nuw/nsw flag inference
strategies.target: SCCP trunc instruction nsw/nuw flag inference
strategies.rationale: The patch adds support for inferring nsw/nuw flags for trunc instructions based on value ranges. This test verifies that flags are correctly inferred when the value range fits within the destination width.
strategies.expected_issue: Correct inference of nsw/nuw flags for trunc instructions

.. _i_trunc:

'``trunc .. to``' Instruction
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

Syntax:
"""""""

::

      <result> = trunc <ty> <value> to <ty2>             ; yields ty2
      <result> = trunc nsw <ty> <value> to <ty2>         ; yields ty2
      <result> = trunc nuw <ty> <value> to <ty2>         ; yields ty2
      <result> = trunc nuw nsw <ty> <value> to <ty2>     ; yields ty2

Overview:
"""""""""

The '``trunc``' instruction truncates its operand to the type ``ty2``.

Arguments:
""""""""""

The '``trunc``' instruction takes a value to trunc, and a type to trunc
it to. Both types must be of :ref:`integer <t_integer>` types, or vectors
of the same number of integers. The bit size of the ``value`` must be
larger than the bit size of the destination type, ``ty2``. Equal sized
types are not allowed.

Semantics:
""""""""""

The '``trunc``' instruction truncates the high order bits in ``value``
and converts the remaining bits to ``ty2``. Since the source size must
be larger than the destination size, ``trunc`` cannot be a *no-op cast*.
It will always truncate bits.

If the ``nuw`` keyword is present, and any of the truncated bits are non-zero,
the result is a :ref:`poison value <poisonvalues>`. If the ``nsw`` keyword
is present, and any of the truncated bits are not the same as the top bit
of the truncation result, the result is a :ref:`poison value <poisonvalues>`.

Example:
""""""""

.. code-block:: llvm

      %X = trunc i32 257 to i8                        ; yields i8:1
      %Y = trunc i32 123 to i1                        ; yields i1:true
      %Z = trunc i32 122 to i1                        ; yields i1:false
      %W = trunc <2 x i16> <i16 8, i16 7> to <2 x i8> ; yields <i8 8, i8 7>

{"test":["```llvm
; Test for SCCP trunc nsw/nuw flag inference
define i8 @test_trunc_flags(i16 %x) {
  ; x is known to be in range [0, 127] which fits in i8 for both signed and unsigned
  %cmp1 = icmp uge i16 %x, 0
  %cmp2 = icmp ule i16 %x, 127
  %and = and i1 %cmp1, %cmp2
  br i1 %and, label %true, label %false

```","opt -passes=ipsccp -S test.ll -o test_opt.ll"],"thoughts":"Bug Triggering Analysis: The patch adds support for inferring nsw/nuw flags for trunc instructions in SCCP. The test case demonstrates that when a value is known to be within a range that fits within the destination width, SCCP correctly infers the appropriate flags. For a value in range [0, 127] being truncated from i16 to i8, both nuw and nsw flags should be added since all values fit within i8 for both signed and unsigned representations.

Fix Weakness Analysis: The patch implementation appears correct. It uses Range.getActiveBits() <= DestWidth to check for nuw (all truncated bits must be zero) and Range.getMinSignedBits() <= DestWidth to check for nsw (truncated bits must equal sign bit). The logic properly handles various range scenarios including wrapped ranges. The early return optimization for instructions that already have both flags set is also correct and doesn't affect correctness. All test cases pass and alive-tv verifies the transformations are correct."}
